name: Apollo Lunar Module
tagline: First crewed lunar lander; Eagle, Antares, Falcon...
dispatch: The Lunar Module was the first true spacecraft — the first crewed vehicle built to fly only in vacuum, never through an atmosphere, so it could throw away streamlining and heat shielding and become exactly what it was: a machine for one job. Grumman split it in two — a descent stage that carried the crew down and then served as the launch pad for a separate ascent stage that carried them back up — because that staging was the only way to close the mass budget for a Moon landing. It flew on spidery legs, its skin in places as thin as a few sheets of foil. Nothing before it had set people on another world, and its ungainly, purpose-built shape is simply what a spacecraft looks like when it never has to survive coming home.
description: The only crewed lunar lander ever built. Six successful landings between 1969 and 1972 — Eagle, Intrepid, Antares, Falcon, Orion, Challenger — plus Aquarius, which served as Apollo 13’s lifeboat. Descent stage stays on the Moon; ascent stage rejoined the CSM in lunar orbit.
